$comment: HTML standards gate declaration (Issue #412). Read by scripts/check-html-standards.mjs and by test/integration/html-standards.test.ts, which drive the same engine (scripts/html-standards-contract.mjs) over the real SSR documents. Severity, the route roster and the waiver ledger live HERE so a policy change is a reviewable diff, not a code change. See docs/verification/standards/html-nu-validator.md.
profile_note: The engine emulates the Nu Html Checker message TYPES (validator.w3.org/nu) for the three defect classes Issue #412 names — invalid markup, duplicate ids, attribute errors — not the whole HTML5 algorithm. It is offline on purpose: validator.nu would upload every rendered document (including /admin pages and their copy) to a third party. The rule ids below map 1:1 onto RULE_CATALOGUE in scripts/html-standards-contract.mjs, and a mismatch in EITHER direction fails the gate.

routes.why: canonical home: the surface every visitor lands on, and the one with the most composed markup (reactions, counter, nav).
person identity surface with structured data and an experience list.
the only form surface; label/for and button/input attributes live here.
the longest public document (a project list), so it is where a nesting or duplicate-id regression would first show.
dynamic detail route; the fixture row is the slug src/portfolio/seed.ts already publishes, so this is a real document and not an empty state.
Tool registry index: the surface with the most external links and iframe-related markup.
the same_origin_static Tool shell that e2e/tools-prototype.spec.ts already loads in a browser.
the editorial primitive gallery: inline SVG, definition lists and the widest attribute surface in the repository, so it is the gate's false-positive canary.
the only admin route an anonymous request can render; the auth gate answers 307 for every other admin URL, so this is where the admin document contract is asserted.

inventory.note: The gate re-derives the published roster from src/routes/** (a file is a route when it calls createFileRoute) and from the generated route tree, and requires this manifest to declare every id in BOTH lists. A route that exists but is not declared fails (inventory.unlisted); a route declared here that no longer exists fails (inventory.missing). An unimplemented route can therefore never pass silently: it has to be rendered and validated, or excluded with a reason.

missing-doctype.reason: SSR renders the doctype; a document without one is in quirks mode and the shipped CSS does not account for it.

bad-doctype.reason: the published document is HTML5; an XHTML or HTML4 doctype would make the browser parse differently from the validator.

obsolete-doctype.reason: a legacy doctype still parses, so this is reported rather than blocking.

missing-element.reason: html / head / body / title are the document skeleton the root route always renders.

duplicate-element.reason: a second <title> or <body> means one of two trees won and the other is dead markup.

missing-attribute.reason: required attributes (html[lang], img[alt], img[src]) are accessibility and language metadata, not decoration.

unknown-attribute.reason: an attribute the element does not accept is a typo or a component prop that leaked into the DOM; React forwards unknown props verbatim.

duplicate-attribute.reason: HTML keeps the first occurrence, so a duplicate silently drops a value a reviewer believed was applied.

bad-value.reason: a boolean/enumerated/ID-valued attribute with a value outside its grammar renders a control the author did not ask for.

duplicate-id.reason: the first duplicate-id defect class in the Issue; every aria-* / label[for] / headers reference resolves to only one of the duplicates.

bad-id.reason: an empty id, or one containing whitespace, cannot be referenced by an IDREF attribute.

bad-idref.reason: an aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / label[for] / td[headers] reference that resolves to nothing is an accessible-name or association bug that no runtime test would catch.

invalid-nesting.reason: the invalid-markup defect class: a block inside a phrasing parent, an interactive control inside a link, an <li> outside a list.

misnested-tag.reason: a misnested pair silently reparents content in the browser, so the rendered DOM is not the authored one.

stray-end-tag.reason: an end tag with no open element is dropped by the parser, which means an unclosed element upstream.

unclosed-element.reason: an element left open at EOF swallows the rest of the document into itself.

empty-title.reason: the <head> contract gate (Issue #418) requires a non-empty title; an empty one would render as a blank SERP entry.

heading-level-skip.reason: a skipped heading level is a document-outline defect for screen-reader navigation, but it does not change what the page means, so it is reported rather than blocking.

fixtures.note: The Issue's first acceptance condition: the invalid fixture MUST fail and the valid fixture MUST pass. The offline mode of the gate asserts exactly that on every run, so a gate that can no longer detect the seeded defects fails instead of reporting green. `expect` lists the rules the invalid fixture is required to produce (each one must appear at least once); `forbidden` lists rules it must NOT produce, which is how a false positive in the engine is caught by its own fixture.

waivers.message_pattern: Element "a" not allowed as child of element "ul"\.
waivers.reason: PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED BY #412 — the desktop public nav (src/editorial/nav/PublicNav.tsx) renders a <ul> whose children are <a> elements with no <li> wrapper, while the mobile list in the same file does wrap them. e2e/nav.spec.ts asserts the '[data-testid="public-nav-desktop"] > a' direct-child selector, so fixing the markup is a coordinated editorial + e2e change and therefore an owner decision, not a gate change. The waiver is scoped to this message shape: any other nesting defect still fails.

waivers.message_pattern: Element "div" not allowed as child of element "button"\.
waivers.reason: PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED BY #412 — the home emoji picker (editorial picker primitives rendered by src/home/reactions/) puts a <div> icon wrapper inside its clear-search <button>; <button> takes phrasing content only. Turning that div into a span is an editorial obligation decision with layout implications for the icon primitive.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED BY #412 — the home emoji picker's search input declares aria-controls="epr-search-id" for a listbox that is mounted client-side only, so the id does not exist in the SSR document. The reference resolves once the picker opens; whether the SSR markup should carry it at all is an editorial decision.
